name: AWS Plugin
description: Instance ID, type, capacity, AMI, on-demand and spot price and launch time of AWS nodes. Works without a login (the cluster's own data plus AWS's public price list); with boto3 and AWS credentials it also shows spot prices, the real launch time and the AMI of every node.

actions.title: Estimate the cost of the selected nodes

settings.label: Use the AWS API when credentials are available
settings.help: Looks up, by instance ID, the AMI the node booted from and its launch time, and current spot prices. It uses boto3 if installed, otherwise the credentials of the AWS CLI (or the AWS_* variables). Untick to use only the cluster and the public price list.

settings.label: AWS profile (default for all clusters)
settings.help: A profile from your AWS config. Empty uses the default credentials.

settings.label: AWS profile for each cluster
settings.help: Clusters in other accounts need their own profile. One per line, as context = profile; the context is the cluster's name in your kubeconfig. A cluster that is not listed uses the default profile above.

settings.label:
Warning: a typed access key is stored unprotected
The key is saved as plain text in Klotse's settings file on this computer. Anyone who can read that file, this computer, or a backup or synced copy of it can use the key. The Klotse authors accept no responsibility for any loss, cost or damage that results from using it: this is your choice and your risk.
Prefer an AWS profile or IAM Identity Center (the AWS CLI keeps those safer). If you do use a key, make it a dedicated read-only one (EC2 describe and STS only), never a root or administrator key, and prefer temporary keys with a session token.
AWS access key ID (optional)
settings.help: Instead of a profile. Needs the secret access key too. When both are filled in they are used for every cluster and replace all profiles. Read the warning above first.

settings.label: AWS secret access key
settings.help: Saved as plain text in the settings file. Read the warning above first.

settings.label: AWS session token (optional)
settings.help: Only for temporary keys (access key IDs starting with ASIA). Leave empty for long-lived keys. Temporary keys expire: paste new ones here when they do.

settings.label: I use several AWS accounts in the console
settings.help: Then "Open in the EC2 console" has to say which account to open. Fill in the three settings below.

settings.label: IAM Identity Center start URL
settings.help: For example https://d-1234567890.awsapps.com/start . The link then signs in to the cluster's account and opens the instance page.

settings.label: Role name
settings.help: With IAM Identity Center: the permission set to sign in with. Without it: a role to switch to (the instance link is put on the clipboard to paste after switching).

settings.label: Sign in to the console automatically (needs boto3 and credentials)
settings.help: Uses your AWS credentials (the profile above) to ask AWS for a one-time sign-in link and opens it in your browser, so there is no login page. The link is never shown, logged or kept. With several accounts it assumes the role named above in the cluster's account. Not used with IAM Identity Center, whose portal signs you in.

settings.label: Account for each cluster
settings.help: Which account a cluster is in, one per line as context = 123456789012. Only needed when the context is not the EKS ARN that 'aws eks update-kubeconfig' creates (it contains the account id).

cluster_settings.label: AWS profile
cluster_settings.help: The profile from your AWS config used for this cluster's EC2 lookups, cost estimate and console sign-in. Empty uses the entry in the plugin's settings, or the default profile.

cluster_settings.label: AWS account ID
cluster_settings.help: Usually leave empty: the account is taken from the plugin's per-cluster list, the EKS ARN in the context name, or else asked from AWS (sts get-caller-identity) for the profile above. Fill it in only to override that.
